{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use Spring Kafka for Kafka integration, leveraging its support for producers, consumers, and configuration.",
    "For Sqoop integration, use Java API or command-line execution via ProcessBuilder to manage jobs and logs.",
    "Implement a hierarchical configuration system with global defaults and per-deployment overrides for Kafka settings.",
    "Use Spring's async support and thread pools for concurrency management in Kafka operations.",
    "Utilize Kafka's built-in compression options (e.g., gzip, snappy) and acknowledgment mechanisms for reliability.",
    "Design the request-reply pattern using correlation IDs and asynchronous messaging to support bindRequestor and bindReplier.",
    "Implement batch processing in Kafka consumers using Spring Kafka's batch listener capabilities.",
    "For Sqoop job control, create a service layer that encapsulates job lifecycle management, including stopping jobs.",
    "Integrate Sqoop logs with the application's logging framework (e.g., SLF4J/Logback) for centralized log access.",
    "Support incremental data load in Sqoop by tracking last import timestamps or using Sqoop's incremental options."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The application is built on Spring Boot, with existing dependencies for Kafka and Sqoop integration.",
    "Development environment includes access to Kafka brokers and Sqoop for testing, with CI infrastructure set up.",
    "Existing application architecture can be extended without major refactoring, focusing on adding new modules or services.",
    "Database connections and Hadoop ecosystem components are configured and available for Sqoop operations.",
    "Unit and integration testing frameworks are in place, and acceptance tests will be written alongside feature development.",
    "The developer is familiar with Spring, Kafka, and Sqoop, and no additional training or learning time is required.",
    "Time estimates include coding, basic testing, and documentation but exclude long-term maintenance or deployment.",
    "Sqoop jobs are run via command-line, and log files are accessible in a standard location or via Sqoop's API."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Kafka Acceptance Test Setup",
      "activity_description": "Develop and configure acceptance tests for Kafka message bus functionality to be executed as part of every CI build, ensuring validation of core features like messaging and reliability.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Kafka Concurrency and Compression Configuration",
      "activity_description": "Implement global default and per-deployment override options for concurrency (e.g., thread count) and compression (e.g., codec settings) in Kafka producers and consumers.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Kafka Message ACK Implementation",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration and handling for message acknowledgment to guarantee successful message sends, integrating with Kafka's acknowledgment levels.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Kafka Request-Reply Pattern Implementation",
      "activity_description": "Implement bindRequestor and bindReplier options to support async request-reply messaging patterns, including correlation ID management and timeout handling.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Kafka Batching Support",
      "activity_description": "Implement support for batch processing of Kafka messages to improve data ingestion efficiency, using batch listeners and configuration for batch sizes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Sqoop Job Stop Service",
      "activity_description": "Develop a service to stop running Sqoop jobs and clean up associated resources, including interaction with Sqoop's job management or process termination.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Sqoop Log Integration",
      "activity_description": "Capture and stream Sqoop logs to the application's logging mechanism for troubleshooting, involving log file monitoring or API integration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Sqoop Incremental Data Load",
      "activity_description": "Implement logic for incremental data loading to retrieve only new rows since the last import, using Sqoop's incremental options or timestamp tracking.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 24
  }
}

Design the request-reply pattern using correlation IDs and asynchronous messaging to support bindRequestor and bindReplier.
Implement batch processing in Kafka consumers using Spring Kafka's batch listener capabilities.
For Sqoop job control, create a service layer that encapsulates job lifecycle management, including stopping jobs.
Integrate Sqoop logs with the application's logging framework (e.g., SLF4J/Logback) for centralized log access.
Support incremental data load in Sqoop by tracking last import timestamps or using Sqoop's incremental options.
assumptions: The application is built on Spring Boot, with existing dependencies for Kafka and Sqoop integration.
Development environment includes access to Kafka brokers and Sqoop for testing, with CI infrastructure set up.
Existing application architecture can be extended without major refactoring, focusing on adding new modules or services.
Database connections and Hadoop ecosystem components are configured and available for Sqoop operations.
Unit and integration testing frameworks are in place, and acceptance tests will be written alongside feature development.
The developer is familiar with Spring, Kafka, and Sqoop, and no additional training or learning time is required.
Time estimates include coding, basic testing, and documentation but exclude long-term maintenance or deployment.
Sqoop jobs are run via command-line, and log files are accessible in a standard location or via Sqoop's API.

activities.activity_description: Develop and configure acceptance tests for Kafka message bus functionality to be executed as part of every CI build, ensuring validation of core features like messaging and reliability.
Implement global default and per-deployment override options for concurrency (e.g., thread count) and compression (e.g., codec settings) in Kafka producers and consumers.
Add configuration and handling for message acknowledgment to guarantee successful message sends, integrating with Kafka's acknowledgment levels.
Implement bindRequestor and bindReplier options to support async request-reply messaging patterns, including correlation ID management and timeout handling.
Implement support for batch processing of Kafka messages to improve data ingestion efficiency, using batch listeners and configuration for batch sizes.
Develop a service to stop running Sqoop jobs and clean up associated resources, including interaction with Sqoop's job management or process termination.
Capture and stream Sqoop logs to the application's logging mechanism for troubleshooting, involving log file monitoring or API integration.
Implement logic for incremental data loading to retrieve only new rows since the last import, using Sqoop's incremental options or timestamp tracking.
